source.english: Ch19.8 PDF40: five or six planets 'normally' indicate adverse outcomes, ascribed to Kandalas; Ch19.1 and 19.7 include distinct favorable outcomes for particular six-planet sets.

sanskrit.semantic_comment: प्रायो (prāyo) = generally/often, not every chart. Verse is qualified, so apparent tension with particular exceptions cannot be called a strict universal contradiction without precedence analysis.

astronomical_method.sample_interval: each Gregorian civil date at 00:00 UTC
astronomical_method.engine: Swiss Ephemeris library via pyswisseph 2.10.03, explicitly FLG_MOSEPH (Moshier, not SWIEPH .se1) | FLG_SIDEREAL
astronomical_method.sign: sidereal 30-degree longitude bins; same-sign proxy, not necessarily same narrow conjunction or unequal-house-system Bhava
astronomical_method.reference_input: Source chapters18–20 refer to together/in one bhava without single uniformly defined orb; this test operationalizes *only* one explicit proxy.

independent_context.role: Community article independently lists April 1821 and February 1962 visible seven-body conjunction episodes; not independent ephemeris parity or any predictive proof.

limitations: Daily 00 UTC samples are neither all possible intra-day instants nor exhaustive root-isolated sign-crossing intervals; short events can be missed.
Moshier calculations are exploratory, NOT canonical verified SWIEPH se1 mode required for the production chart engine.
Sidereal same-sign inclusion does NOT imply a narrow angular conjunction and may differ from quadrant-house Bhava.
Past 400-year days are not a random independent participant sample; multi-day episodes and nested five/six subgroups are correlated.
Source Sanskrit digitization and English translation may share a printed ancestor. Precise classical conjunction threshold remains unresolved.
An occurrence of a configuration does not mean the predicted wealth, profession, religion or mortality actually followed.
model_impact: No production changes. A candidate model must freeze same-sign versus Bhava versus angular-orb and issue one outcome vector per event, not every nested combination as separate success.
